However, operation on 'a' turns it into 'z' which is huge (bad). So we want to avoid turning any 'a' into 'z' because that increases the string lexicographically.

Thus we want to apply operation on a substring that contains no 'a's (i.e., all characters > 'a') to get them decreased; decreasing them makes them lexicographically smaller. For characters > 'a', decreasing them yields a letter earlier in alphabet, which is beneficial. For 'a', decreasing yields 'z', which is bad.
